VERDICT: REJECT

The reasoning does not establish the bound. The claim that "the average valency never needs to exceed 6" is asserted, not proved. The Euler-characteristic count $E - V = 2g-2+m$ only fixes the average valency $2E/V$ for a given quiver. It does not force any vertex-valency bound, and the "trade high-valent vertices" step is not explained. The lower-bound argument has the same gap: it says some spaces force average valency above 5, but average valency above 5 does not imply a vertex of valency 6 is needed.

I also don't have a reliable recollection of the sharp constant from the literature on ribbon quivers and pre-Calabi–Yau structures (the Kontsevich–Takeda–Vlassopoulos line of work). My recollection is that the sharp valency bound in that setting is smaller than 6, possibly 4, but I can't confirm that. So the rejection rests mainly on the unjustified argument, not on a known value.

CONFIDENCE: 2
